title: Five Taiwanese Cacao Farmers Will Compete at a World Chocolate Contest
summaryZh: 五位台灣可可農將代表參加國際可可大賽
summaryHi: पाँच ताइवानी कोको किसान 2027 की विश्व कोको प्रतियोगिता में ताइवान का प्रतिनिधित्व करेंगे।
summaryEs: Cinco cacaoteros taiwaneses representarán a Taiwán en el concurso mundial de cacao de 2027.

summaryEn: Five Taiwanese cacao farmers have been chosen to represent Taiwan at the 2027 world cacao competition.
paragraphs: Five Taiwanese cacao growers have been selected to represent the country at the 2027 Cacao of Excellence (CoEx), a major international competition held every two years. To take part in the global event, farmers must first stand out in a national contest, and the Pingtung County government announced Taiwan's winners on October 25.

Thirty samples of cacao beans were entered in this year's Taiwan competition. Before any tasting took place, the beans were tested for physical quality, moisture content and pesticide residues. Only 13 samples made it through to the sensory stage.

To ensure a fair comparison, all 13 were roasted, ground and tempered using the same standard method and turned into cocoa paste and thin pieces of chocolate. Judges then scored them on aroma, acidity, bitterness and astringency, following international CoEx standards.

The gold award went to Mo Chia-wei of Laomo Cocoa in Pingtung County, the heart of Taiwan's cacao industry. Shih Shu-chin of Changhua County took silver, Lin Cheng-hung of Nantou County won bronze, and two more Pingtung farmers received honourable mentions.

Taiwan has a good record at the event, having won two silver awards and one bronze in 2025. The public will be able to taste the results, as chocolate made from the 13 finalists will be displayed at the Taiwan International Coffee Show from November 13 to 16.
Chocolate comes from cacao beans. Cacao trees grow in hot places. Some farmers in Taiwan grow cacao too, most of them in Pingtung County in the south.
This month, Taiwan had a cacao contest. Farmers sent 30 bags of beans. First, experts checked the beans. Then 13 were made into chocolate, and judges tasted it.
Mo Chia-wei from Pingtung won the gold prize. A farmer from Changhua won silver, and a farmer from Nantou won bronze. Two more farmers from Pingtung also got prizes.
These five farmers will go to a big world contest in 2027. It is called Cacao of Excellence. It happens every two years. In 2025, Taiwan won two silver prizes and one bronze prize there.
People can see chocolate from the 13 best beans at a coffee show in November.

Five cacao farmers have been chosen to represent Taiwan at the 2027 Cacao of Excellence, an important world competition for the beans that are used to make chocolate. The Pingtung County government announced the results on October 25.

The farmers were picked through a national contest. Thirty samples of cacao beans were sent in. Experts first tested them for quality, water content and chemicals used on farms. Only 13 samples passed these tests.

Those 13 samples were then made into cocoa paste and thin pieces of chocolate in the same way, so that the judges could compare them fairly. The judges looked at smell, sourness, bitterness and how dry the chocolate felt in the mouth.
The gold prize went to Mo Chia-wei of Laomo Cocoa in Pingtung County. Farmers from Changhua and Nantou won silver and bronze, and two more Pingtung farmers received special prizes.
Taiwan won two silver awards and one bronze at the last world contest in 2025. Chocolate made from the 13 best beans will be shown at the Taiwan International Coffee Show from November 13 to 16.

Five Taiwanese cacao growers have been selected to represent the country at the 2027 Cacao of Excellence (CoEx), a major international competition held every two years. To take part in the global event, farmers must first stand out in a national contest, and the Pingtung County government announced Taiwan's winners on October 25.

Thirty samples of cacao beans were entered in this year's Taiwan competition. Before any tasting took place, the beans were tested for physical quality, moisture content and pesticide residues. Only 13 samples made it through to the sensory stage.

To ensure a fair comparison, all 13 were roasted, ground and tempered using the same standard method and turned into cocoa paste and thin pieces of chocolate. Judges then scored them on aroma, acidity, bitterness and astringency, following international CoEx standards.

The gold award went to Mo Chia-wei of Laomo Cocoa in Pingtung County, the heart of Taiwan's cacao industry. Shih Shu-chin of Changhua County took silver, Lin Cheng-hung of Nantou County won bronze, and two more Pingtung farmers received honourable mentions.

Taiwan has a good record at the event, having won two silver awards and one bronze in 2025. The public will be able to taste the results, as chocolate made from the 13 finalists will be displayed at the Taiwan International Coffee Show from November 13 to 16.

Taiwan may not be the first place that comes to mind when people think of chocolate, but its cacao growers are steadily earning international recognition. Five farmers have now been selected to represent the country at the 2027 Cacao of Excellence (CoEx), a prestigious biennial competition for which entrants must first distinguish themselves at national level.

The selection process, announced by the Pingtung County government on October 25, was rigorous. Of the 30 bean samples submitted, only 13 survived initial screening for physical quality, moisture content and pesticide residues and advanced to sensory evaluation.

To remove any variation in processing, the finalists' beans were roasted, ground and tempered under standardised conditions before being turned into cocoa paste and thin chocolate pieces. Judges then assessed aroma, acidity, bitterness and astringency in line with CoEx criteria.

Mo Chia-wei of Laomo Cocoa in Pingtung County, the centre of Taiwan's cacao cultivation, claimed the gold award. Shih Shu-chin of Changhua County and Lin Cheng-hung of Nantou County took silver and bronze respectively, while two further Pingtung growers received honourable mentions.

Taiwan's earlier haul of two silvers and a bronze at the 2025 awards suggests the island's small-scale producers can hold their own internationally. Chocolate made from all 13 finalists will be showcased at the Taiwan International Coffee Show from November 13 to 16.

Although Taiwan is better known for semiconductors and bubble tea than for chocolate, the island's cacao sector is gradually gaining a reputation abroad. Five Taiwanese farmers have been chosen to compete at the 2027 Cacao of Excellence (CoEx), a prestigious biennial contest that admits only producers who have already excelled in national competitions.

The domestic selection, announced by the Pingtung County government on October 25, was notably demanding. Thirty bean samples were submitted, yet merely 13 passed preliminary tests assessing physical quality, moisture content and pesticide residues, thereby qualifying for sensory evaluation.

Crucially, the organisers sought to eliminate any differences arising from processing. Every finalist's beans were roasted, ground and tempered according to an identical, standardised procedure and then transformed into cocoa paste and thin chocolate pieces. This meant that the judges, who evaluated aroma, acidity, bitterness and astringency in accordance with CoEx criteria, were comparing the intrinsic quality of the beans rather than the skill of a chocolate maker.

The gold award was won by Mo Chia-wei of Laomo Cocoa in Pingtung County, which is widely regarded as the hub of Taiwan's cacao cultivation. Silver and bronze went to growers from Changhua and Nantou counties respectively, while two other Pingtung farmers received honourable mentions.

Given that Taiwan secured two silver awards and a bronze in 2025, there is reason for optimism. Meanwhile, chocolate produced from all 13 finalists will be exhibited at the Taiwan International Coffee Show from November 13 to 16.

note.meaning: 名聲。文中指台灣可可在國際上逐漸建立名聲。
note.usage: gain/build/earn a reputation (for sth)；a reputation as …。

example.en: The town has a reputation for excellent seafood.
example.zh: 這個小鎮以優質海鮮聞名。

noteEn.meaning: the opinion that people have about someone or something.
noteEn.usage: 'gain a reputation for sth'; 'a reputation as...'.

noteHi.meaning: लोगों की किसी के बारे में राय; प्रतिष्ठा।
noteHi.exampleTr: यह कस्बा बेहतरीन समुद्री भोजन के लिए प्रसिद्ध है।

noteEs.meaning: opinión que la gente tiene de algo.
noteEs.exampleTr: El pueblo tiene fama por su excelente marisco.

noteJa.usage: gain a reputation for 〜 の形が多い。
noteJa.exampleTr: その町は海産物の美味しさで評判だ。

noteKo.usage: gain a reputation for ~ 형태로 쓴다.

respectively.en: in the same order as just mentioned
respectively.ex: Tom and Ann are 10 and 12 respectively.

results.ex: The test results came out today.

rigorous.ex: New drugs go through rigorous testing.

note.meaning: 嚴格的；嚴謹的。文中指台灣選拔過程嚴格。
note.usage: a rigorous process/test/standard；強調仔細且要求高。

example.en: All new medicines go through rigorous testing.
example.zh: 所有新藥都要經過嚴格測試。

noteEn.usage: 'a rigorous process/test'; stresses care and high standards.

noteHi.exampleTr: सभी नई दवाओं का सख़्त परीक्षण होता है।

noteEs.exampleTr: Todos los medicamentos nuevos pasan pruebas rigurosas.

noteJa.usage: a rigorous process/test の形が多い。
noteJa.exampleTr: 新薬はすべて厳格な試験を受ける。

roasted.ex: The coffee beans were roasted that morning.

samples.en: early examples of a product for testing
samples.ex: The factory sent samples to customers.

scored.en: gave points to show how good something is
scored.ex: The teacher scored each essay out of ten.

screening.ex: Screening at the border is strict.

sector.en: a part of a country's economy
sector.ex: The public sector employs many nurses.

secured.ex: The club secured a new sponsor.

see.ex: Let's see if the shop is open.

selected.ex: Five farmers were selected for the team.

selection.ex: The selection was made by experts.

semiconductors.en: materials or chips used in electronics

sensory.en: relating to taste, smell, sight, touch or sound
sensory.ex: The sensory test checks taste and smell.

sent.ex: She sent the photo to her friend.

showcased.ex: Local food will be showcased at the fair.

shown.en: put somewhere for people to see
shown.ex: The paintings will be shown in May.

shu-chin.en: part of the name Shih Shu-chin, a cacao farmer

silver.ex: She won silver in the swimming race.

silvers.ex: The team won two silvers and a bronze.

smell.en: what you notice with your nose
smell.ex: I love the smell of coffee.

so.ex: It was raining, so we stayed home.

some.en: a number of, but not all

sought.en: asked for or tried to get
sought.ex: She sought advice from a lawyer.

sourness.ex: Lemons are known for their sourness.

south.ex: Birds fly to the south in winter.

special.en: different and given for a reason
special.ex: He got a special prize for effort.

stage.en: a point in a process or time
stage.ex: At this stage, it is too early to say.

stand.en: (stand out) to be clearly better than others
stand.ex: Good students stand out in class.

standard.ex: This is a standard size for printer paper.

standardised.en: made the same according to fixed rules
standardised.ex: All students take a standardised test.

standards.en: levels of quality that are expected
standards.ex: The hotel has very high standards.

submitted.ex: She submitted her report on time.

suggests.en: shows that something is probably true
suggests.ex: The data suggests people are buying less.

survived.ex: Only three plants survived the winter.

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

take.ex: Ireland will take part in EU missions.

taste.en: to try food or drink in your mouth
taste.ex: You can taste the cake for free.

tasted.en: tried food or drink in the mouth

tasting.en: trying food or drink to judge it
tasting.ex: The wine tasting starts at six.

tea.en: a hot or cold drink made from leaves
tea.ex: Would you like some green tea?

tempered.en: (chocolate) heated and cooled carefully to make it shiny
tempered.ex: The chocolate was tempered so it would shine.

tested.en: checked carefully to find out quality
tested.ex: The water was tested for chemicals.

tests.en: checks to find out quality or safety
tests.ex: All toys must pass safety tests.

themselves.en: without anyone doing it; on their own

then.ex: First read the text, then answer the questions.

there.ex: We went to the park and played there.

thereby.ex: He saved money, thereby avoiding debt.

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

thin.ex: Cut the bread into thin slices.

think.ex: Experts think a deal is possible.

through.ex: They bought it through a special deal.

took.ex: She took silver in the race.

transformed.ex: The old factory was transformed into flats.

trees.ex: Strong winds brought down many trees.

turned.ex: The milk was turned into cheese.

under.en: in a particular situation or with certain rules

used.en: put into service for a purpose
used.ex: The old bricks were used again.

using.ex: Using a map helped us find the hotel.

variation.ex: There is a lot of variation in prices.

water.ex: Do not drive through deep water.

way.ex: Do it the same way every time.

went.ex: First prize went to a girl from Tainan.

were.ex: The shops were closed on Sunday.

widely.ex: Opinions on the plan differ widely.

will.en: used to talk about the future
will.ex: The new bridge will open next year.

winners.ex: The winners will get a prize.

won.ex: Our team won the cup last year.

world.en: the earth and all its countries
world.ex: She wants to travel around the world.

yet.ex: The cost is not yet known.
